result:
No fixed pixel widths that could overflow — everything uses relative units, `clamp()`, `ch`, and percentage/grid layouts, so 390 px and 1440 px should both render without horizontal scroll. The build is complete.

I built Ferrymead Bakehouse as a restrained editorial page around one visual idea: the estuary itself, rendered as three thin SVG tide-line waves layered behind the hero headline that drift at slightly different rates on scroll (a genuine parallax, transform-only, capped and disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`). The palette is four colours — ink `#1b2b2f`, paper `#f4ede1`, rust `#8a3a1c`, and a muted tide teal `#33504a` — paired with a warm serif (Georgia/Iowan) for headlines, system sans for body copy, and a monospace accent for timetable-style labels (weights, step numbers, the 1911/1974/2019 timeline), echoing the old ferry terminal's departures-board character. Each section carries exactly one motion idea: the loaves list staggers in via IntersectionObserver reveals, the subscription heading sticks in a CSS-only grid as its three steps scroll past, and the hall's timeline line draws itself with a `scaleX` transform between the three dates; Visit and the footer stay still, giving the page a settling, unhurried close. All copy is verbatim, everything is readable and fully laid out with JavaScript disabled (the reveal system's default/no-JS state is 100% opacity, no transform — JS only adds the entrance animation), there's a skip link, semantic landmarks, one `h1`, focus-visible outlines, and no external resources of any kind; I verified the exact copy strings render in the page text and confirmed no fixed pixel widths or off-viewport positioning that could cause overflow or clipping at 390 px or 1440 px.
